cycles.en_text_before_rewrite:
# I Followed an AI Phone Agent and Found a Human

The AI makes the call. The user asks it to handle a task. So who is actually speaking on the other end?

A story about Meta’s AI agent, Muse, has emerged that feels like looking behind the scenes.

Muse can call businesses and stores in the United States. It can make a haircut appointment, ask about products in stock, or get a price quote from a service provider. The system lets AI handle troublesome calls for the user.

But unexpected performers appeared in some of the calls. They were not AI, but trained human contract workers. A test was carried out in which workers took over from Muse, made the actual calls, and finished the conversations with the other party.

In other words, although it looked like an AI phone service, a human was handling the call behind the scenes. If you thought the AI was making the call on its own, a human helper had stepped in from the side of the stage. That was the twist.

But this was not just a comedy. Depending on the call, the user’s sensitive information may be needed. Meta employees raised privacy concerns over the possibility that this information could be shared unintentionally with contract workers at a call center.

This does not mean that a large data leak occurred. The problem was that testing began without a proper explanation that humans would handle the calls or that information might be shared.

A Meta executive in charge admitted that this was a “mistake.” The human concierge feature was temporarily rolled back. The phone feature as a whole was not stopped.

Meta says it will continue improving the service with businesses and will make it available to the public only when it is ready and can provide proper disclosure.

The new thing to check when asking AI to make a call is surprisingly simple: Is the voice we are talking to now an AI or a human? The more convenient the phone service, the more we want it to properly introduce even the last performer to appear. This incident brought those behind-the-scenes rules into the open in a striking way.

## In one line
During testing, Meta’s AI phone agent sometimes had human contractors make calls without properly telling users.

In other words, although it looked like an AI phone service, a human was handling the call behind the scenes. If you thought the AI was making the call on its own, a human helper had stepped in from the side of the stage. That was the twist.

But this was not just a comedy. Depending on the call, the user’s sensitive information may be needed. Meta employees raised privacy concerns over the possibility that this information could be shared unintentionally with contract workers at a call center.

This does not mean that a large data leak occurred. The problem was that testing began without a proper explanation that humans would handle the calls.

A Meta executive in charge admitted that this was a “mistake.” The human concierge feature was temporarily rolled back. The phone feature as a whole was not stopped.

Meta says it will continue improving the service with businesses and will make it available to the public only when it is ready and can provide proper disclosure.

en_title_changes.before: # I Followed an AI Phone Agent and Found a Human

verdicts.claim: # I Followed an AI Phone Agent and Found a Human
verdicts.reason: 見出しは書き手自身がAIエージェントを追い、人間を発見したという具体的な行動を述べており、Ledgerでは裏付けられていない。
Museの電話機能は裏付けられるが、Ledgerは一部の電話を人間が担当したと限定しており、AIが電話を担当するとの無限定な記述は範囲と限定条件を広げている。

verdicts.claim: So who is actually speaking on the other end?
verdicts.reason: 誰が話しているのかを尋ねる修辞的な問いで、具体的な事実を追加していない。

verdicts.claim: The system lets AI handle troublesome calls for the user.
verdicts.reason: Museがユーザーの依頼で企業や店舗に電話し、用件を処理できるというLedgerの説明の範囲内である。

verdicts.claim: But unexpected performers appeared in some of the calls.
verdicts.reason: 一部の電話でAIではなく訓練を受けた人間が担当したというLedgerの記述と一致する。「予想外」は評価的表現である。

verdicts.claim: In other words, although it looked like an AI phone service, a human was handling the call behind the scenes.
verdicts.reason: 人間が電話を担当した事実は裏付けられるが、Ledgerの「一部の電話」「テスト」という限定が落ちているため、範囲と限定条件が不一致。

verdicts.claim: If you thought the AI was making the call on its own, a human helper had stepped in from the side of the stage.
verdicts.reason: 人間がMuseに代わって電話を担当した事実は裏付けられるが、「一部の電話」「テスト」という限定が落ちている。

verdicts.claim: This does not mean that a large data leak occurred.
verdicts.reason: Ledgerはプライバシー上の懸念を記録しつつ、大規模な情報漏えいが起きたと断定しないよう明記しており、記事も発生を断定していない。

verdicts.claim: The problem was that testing began without a proper explanation that humans would handle the calls or that information might be shared.
verdicts.reason: 人間が電話を担当することについて適切な開示がなかった点は裏付けられるが、情報共有の可能性についても説明がなかったとする限定的な新事実まではLedgerで確認できない。

verdicts.claim: A Meta executive in charge admitted that this was a “mistake.”
verdicts.reason: Metaの幹部が、適切な開示なしにテストを始めたことを「ミス」と認めたというLedgerの記述と一致する。

verdicts.claim: The new thing to check when asking AI to make a call is surprisingly simple: Is the voice we are talking to now an AI or a human?
verdicts.reason: 電話相手がAIか人間かという点を読者に問いかける助言的・修辞的表現で、具体的な事実を追加していない。

verdicts.claim: The more convenient the phone service, the more we want it to properly introduce even the last performer to appear.
verdicts.reason: 望ましい開示についての論評・要望であり、具体的な事実の主張ではない。

verdicts.claim: During testing, Meta’s AI phone agent sometimes had human contractors make calls without properly telling users.
verdicts.reason: テスト中の一部の電話を契約スタッフが担当し、適切な開示がなかったというLedgerの内容を、範囲を保って要約している。

verdicts.claim: So who is actually speaking on the other end?
verdicts.reason: C3と同じ修辞的な問いであり、具体的な事実を追加していない。
